prompts.display_text: Pin a country with 500,000 or more Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.text_original: Pin a country with 500,000 or more Church members (end of 2025).
prompts.summary: At the end of 2025 seven countries had 500,000 or more Church members. The United States led with about 6.93 million, followed by Brazil and Mexico at about 1.57 million each, then the Philippines, Peru, Chile and Argentina.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: About 1.57 million members, just ahead of Mexico.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: About 1.57 million members.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: About 6.93 million members.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: About 905,000 members.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: About 506,000 members.

answers.name: Chile
answers.fact: About 624,000 members.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: About 668,000 members.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a city Solomon built, or the homeland of one of his wives or royal allies (not Sheba)
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a city Solomon built or fortified, or the homeland of one of his wives or royal allies (Kings and Chronicles; not the queen of Sheba). Trade lands of disputed site, such as Ophir and Tarshish, are not asked.
prompts.note: Jerusalem is scored as Israel, as in the other Bible prompts; Beth-horon the nether is in the West Bank.
prompts.summary: Solomon fortified Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer, built Tadmor and store cities in Hamath, and traded cedar with Hiram of Tyre. He married Pharaoh's daughter and many foreign wives from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zidon and the Hittites (1 Kgs 3-11; 2 Chr 8-9).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Solomon built Hazor, Megiddo and Gezer (1 Kgs 9:15) and the temple at Jerusalem.

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: He married Pharaoh's daughter, who brought Gezer as a dowry (1 Kgs 3:1; 9:16).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Hiram king of Tyre sent cedars of Lebanon for the temple, and Solomon loved women of the Zidonians (1 Kgs 5:1-10; 11:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: He loved women of the Moabites, Ammonites and Edomites (1 Kgs 11:1); Naamah the Ammonitess bore Rehoboam (1 Kgs 14:21).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: He built Tadmor in the wilderness and store cities in Hamath (2 Chr 8:3-4).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: He built Beth-horon the nether, now in the West Bank (1 Kgs 9:17).

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: He loved Hittite women (1 Kgs 11:1); the Bible Dictionary says the Hittite empire reached into Asia Minor.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country bordering France (overseas France included) with a temple dedicated, under construction or announced.
prompts.text_original: A country that shares a land border with France (overseas France included: French Guiana and Saint Martin) and has a temple at any stage, dedicated, under construction or announced (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronology (dedicated, under construction, announced), read 27 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Of France's land neighbours, Germany, Spain, Italy and Switzerland have dedicated temples and Belgium has one under construction in Brussels. The surprise is Brazil: French Guiana is part of France, so France's longest land border is with Brazil, which has twelve dedicated temples. Luxembourg, Monaco, Andorra and Suriname have none.

answers.name: Germany
answers.fact: Freiberg 1985, Frankfurt 1987, Hamburg announced.

answers.name: Spain
answers.fact: Madrid 1999; Barcelona under construction.

answers.name: Italy
answers.fact: Rome 2019; Milan announced.

answers.name: Switzerland
answers.fact: Bern Switzerland Temple dedicated 1955.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: Brussels Belgium Temple under construction.

answers.name: Netherlands
answers.fact: The Kingdom of the Netherlands borders France on Saint Martin/Sint Maarten; The Hague Netherlands Temple dedicated 2002.

answers.name: Brazil
answers.fact: Brazil borders French Guiana; São Paulo 1978 and eleven more temples.

prompts.text_original: A Central American country (Guatemala to Panama) where the Church has 5 or more stakes as of October 2026.
prompts.citation: Church facts and statistics country pages (figures of 31 Dec 2025), read 4 Nov 2026
prompts.summary: Six of the seven Central American countries have 5 or more stakes: Guatemala (51), Honduras (31), El Salvador (22), Nicaragua (12), Costa Rica (10) and Panama (7). Belize, the smallest, has a district but no stake.

answers.name: Guatemala
answers.fact: 51 stakes; about 297,000 members.

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: 31 stakes; about 197,000 members.

answers.name: El Salvador
answers.fact: 22 stakes; about 132,000 members.

answers.name: Costa Rica
answers.fact: 10 stakes; about 58,000 members.

answers.name: Nicaragua
answers.fact: 12 stakes; about 107,000 members.

answers.name: Panama
answers.fact: 7 stakes; about 64,000 members.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country whose official or national language received its first complete Book of Mormon during the 1990s.
prompts.text_original: The 1990s brought first complete Book of Mormon editions in several languages, from Hungarian (1991) to Haitian Creole (1999). Pin a country where an official or national language received its first complete Book of Mormon in the 1990s.
prompts.citation: Global Histories chronologies: Hungary, Ukraine, Romania, Albania, Bulgaria, Zimbabwe, Haiti, Philippines
prompts.summary: As the Church entered Eastern Europe after 1989, the Book of Mormon followed: Hungarian in 1991, Ukrainian in 1997, Romanian in 1998, Albanian and Bulgarian in 1999. The same decade brought full editions in Shona for Zimbabwe, Haitian Creole for Haiti and three Philippine languages in 1998.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Complete Tagalog, Cebuano and Pangasinan editions were published in 1998.

answers.name: Haiti
answers.fact: The complete Haitian Creole translation was published in 1999.

answers.name: Hungary
answers.fact: The Hungarian Book of Mormon was distributed in December 1991.

answers.name: Ukraine
answers.fact: The Ukrainian Book of Mormon was published in 1997.

answers.name: Albania
answers.fact: The Albanian Book of Mormon became available in November 1999.

answers.name: Bulgaria
answers.fact: The Bulgarian Book of Mormon was published in 1999.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: A complete Romanian translation was published in October 1998.

answers.name: Zimbabwe
answers.fact: The first full Shona edition was published in 1999.

answers.name: Moldova
answers.fact: Romanian, Moldova's official language, received its complete Book of Mormon in 1998.
